version.changelog: Security fix: removed hardcoded credentials from defaults. Credentials now required via environment variables.

llm.summary: The code implements a legitimate Omie API client and webhook receiver, but the package metadata omits the required OMIE credentials and the webhook server binds to all interfaces and logs events to disk — these inconsistencies and exposure risks warrant caution.

dimensions.detail: Code and SKILL.md implement an Omie API client (clients, products, orders, NF-e, finance, stock) and a webhook receiver — this matches the skill description. However, the registry metadata claims 'Required env vars: none' while SKILL.md and the code require OMIE_APP_KEY and OMIE_APP_SECRET. That mismatch is an incoherence between declared requirements and actual capability.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md instructs the agent/user to export OMIE_APP_KEY and OMIE_APP_SECRET and to run the included Python scripts; the scripts perform only Omie API calls and local logging. However the webhook receiver writes incoming event payloads to a local events file and exposes a /events endpoint that returns recent events — this means incoming webhook payloads (which may contain sensitive customer/financial data) will be persisted and served over HTTP. The runtime behavior (logging and exposing events) is not prominently warned in the SKILL.md and could be surprising to operators.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec or external downloads; this is an instruction-only skill with included Python scripts. No third-party packages or remote installers are pulled — low install-time risk.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The code legitimately uses OMIE_APP_KEY and OMIE_APP_SECRET to authenticate to app.omie.com.br, which is proportionate to the described purpose. However, the registry metadata omits these required environment variables, creating an inconsistency that could mislead users or automated permission checks. No other unrelated credentials are requested.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The webhook server defaults to binding host 0.0.0.0 (all interfaces) unless overridden, which exposes endpoints (webhook receiver, /events, /health) to the network by default. It also persists raw event data to a logs/webhook_events.jsonl file and serves recent events via /events. Defaulting to public binding plus persistent logging increases the attack surface and risk of data exposure if deployed without proper network controls.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to implement a real Omie API client and webhook receiver, but there are actionable issues you should address before deploying: 1) Provide OMIE_APP_KEY and OMIE_APP_SECRET only if you trust the code and understand what data will be accessed; the skill will call app.omie.com.br using those credentials. 2) The registry metadata incorrectly lists no required env vars — treat that as a red flag and prefer skills that declare needed credentials. 3) The webhook server defaults to binding 0.0.0.0 and will persist incoming webhook payloads to logs/webhook_events.jsonl and expose them via /events; run it behind a firewall or bind to localhost (use --host 127.0.0.1) and restrict access, or remove/secure the /events endpoint before exposing to the internet. 4) Review the scripts yourself (or have someone you trust do so) before supplying production credentials, and consider creating a least-privilege Omie app or test account for evaluation. 5) Ask the publisher to update registry metadata to declare the required env vars and to document the webhook server's default host binding and logging behavior.
